q: The Hadamard-Perron method proves the stable manifold theorem using a fixed-point argument. The stable manifold near a hyperbolic fixed point is constructed as a graph over E^s of a Lipschitz function h: E^s → E^u. The map h is a fixed point of the:
opts: Graph transform operator Γ, which sends a graph h to the graph of a new function computed by one step of the dynamics and projection
exp: Graph transform: Γ sends a Lipschitz graph h: E^s → E^u to the graph of T∘h∘(T|_{E^s})⁻¹ (apply T, project back). The hyperbolicity ensures Γ is a contraction on the space of Lipschitz graphs, giving a unique fixed point h that is the stable manifold. This is the Perron-Irwin method.
